basics.name: Ayesh Abu Lehyeh
basics.label: PhD Researcher | Computer Vision & Geolocalization
basics.summary: PhD researcher at the University of Vermont specializing in computer vision and machine learning for geolocalization. My research focuses on fine-grained and reliable geolocalization from visual and sensor data, with an emphasis on uncertainty modeling, cross-view reasoning, and real-world deployment constraints.

work.name: University of Vermont
highlights: Conducting PhD research on machine learning–based geolocalization, with a primary focus on computer vision, spatial reasoning, and uncertainty-aware modeling
Project 1 — GPS-Free Geolocalization for Outdoor Sensor Networks:
Designed a geolocalization framework for large-scale outdoor IoT sensor networks without relying on GPS, using only inter-node radio range measurements
Developed a spatio-temporal learning framework combining Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and BiLSTMs to model spatial topology and temporal dynamics
Achieved meter-level localization accuracy in noisy outdoor environments relevant to smart cities and real-world deployments
This work resulted in a peer-reviewed publication in an IoT journal (see Publications section)
Project 2 — Reliable Indoor Geolocalization with Uncertainty Guarantees:
Developed a GNN-based regression model for indoor geolocalization predicting continuous spatial coordinates
Integrated conformal prediction to produce statistically valid confidence regions with reliable coverage guarantees
Demonstrated strong uncertainty calibration, with empirical coverage closely matching target confidence levels
Project page: https://ayeshabulehyeh.github.io/projects/2_project/
Project 3 — Visual Geolocalization under Severe Weather and Appearance Changes:
Studied the robustness of image-based geolocalization under severe weather, illumination, and seasonal changes
Extended the Sample4Geo baseline with improved training strategies and robustness-oriented evaluation protocols
Identified and quantified failure modes of visual geolocalization models under extreme appearance shifts
Project 4 — Efficient Fine-Grained Cross-View Image Geolocalization:
Developed an efficient cross-view geolocalization framework aligning ground-level and satellite imagery
Designed architectures that decouple heavy visual encoding from fast geometric refinement for real-time inference
Achieved sub-meter–level geolocalization accuracy with significantly reduced inference cost compared to prior methods
This work is currently under review at a top-tier computer vision venue
Ongoing Work — Vision-Language Models for Geolocalization Reasoning:
Exploring vision-language models for semantic and spatial reasoning in geolocalization tasks
Evaluating prompting strategies and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) for location reasoning and interpretability
All research implemented primarily in PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric, with rigorous experimentation, ablation studies, and reproducibility practices
